text:
maria_engineering: Seeing a hard throughput drop on eu-west cluster since ~08:10 UTC. p50 latency is fine but p95/p99 spiked and tail tokens per second collapsed. Noticed a wave of worker restarts and a few GPU OOM events.
soham_ml: Any recent rollouts or kernel changes?
maria_engineering: We rolled kernel-selection heuristic rollout (v2) at 07:58 — it biases small-batch fast-kernels for short sequences. Could that interact with KV cache usage?
louis_infra: Oncall saw auto-restarts due to CUDA OOMs between 08:06-08:12. Attaching snippet from node logs: 

```
[08:06:14] worker-37: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[08:06:14] worker-37: traceback: runtime::alloc -> gpu_allocator.cu:237
[08:07:01] worker-12: eviction: kicked kvcache slab id=5 size=1.2GB
[08:08:03] orchestrator: restarting worker-37 (oom)
```

karen_oncall: I restarted one host at 08:13 after flapping. We had repeated slab eviction/alloc churn reported. Could be memory fragmentation after kernel switch.
maria_engineering: Perf-bot, can you paste the profiling summary for kernels and batch sizes around the window 07:50-08:20?
perf-bot: summary: total requests 1.2M, overall tokens/s down 62% vs baseline. Kernel selection changed: small-kernel winrate +42% on short seqs, large-kernel fallback +30% on medium seqs. KV cache hit rate dropped from 84% -> 61% after 08:00. Hotpage fragmentation metric increased by 18%.
soham_ml: KV hit rate drop seems suspicious. If prefix eviction/pinning changed due to kernel memory patterns, we could be thrashing the cache and forcing full attention allocations.
louis_infra: I'm seeing increased per-worker peak resident set before OOMs: 14.2GB -> 19.8GB on 24GB cards, with many small allocations (4k-256k) causing allocator slab fragmentation.
maria_engineering: Can we get a sample stack of allocations causing fragmentation? karen, any logs for allocator metrics?
karen_oncall: Pasted allocator metrics from the cluster during spike: 

```
ALLOC_STATS(timestamp=08:05)
  allocated_bytes: 12.9GB
  free_slabs: 3
  largest_free_block: 512KB
  reclaim_attempts: 11
  kvcache_evictions: 42
  small_alloc_count(<=64k): 1.3M
```

soham_ml: That largest_free_block looks tiny. Suggests external fragmentation. Could kernel selection be switching to kernels that allocate many temporary buffers per token? We changed attention workspace allocation in v2.
maria_engineering: I pushed a quick revert of kernel-selection heuristics at 08:25 to stop the new kernel being chosen. After revert, requests/s started recovering slowly.
louis_infra: Confirmed: after 08:30, worker restarts reduced and KV hit rate climbed back to ~79% by 08:40. p95 improved but still ~12% worse than baseline.
soham_ml: We should capture per-kernel temporary allocation profile and a timeline of kvcache evictions. Also need to audit attention workspace growth with batch size.
maria_engineering: Agreed. Action items: 1) run microprofiler collecting per-kernel alloc/free counts for next rollout (assigned to soham). 2) Add a safeguard in scheduler to avoid switching kernel families if kvcache fragmentation > threshold (assigned to louis). 3) Add e2e test that simulates heavy prefix reuse to catch kv hit-rate regressions (assigned to maria).
maria_engineering: Quick note for postmortem: root cause seems interaction of kernel-selection heuristic + attention workspace allocations causing small-block allocator fragmentation leading to kvcache evictions -> increased full allocations -> GPU OOM -> worker restarts -> throughput collapse.
karen_oncall: Logged incident on PagerDuty and attached relevant graphs (oom_count, kv_hit_rate, tokens_per_sec). I'm keeping this thread open; ping me if you need node-level traces. :thumbsup:
